title: VXAce Things that worked suddenly don't

posts.author: EntangledPear
posts.body: I feel just about ready to give up, with the game about 90% done. Little things started not working - a light event that works on five maps doesn't work on three others. A save game file that doesn't show up to be loaded, but can't be deleted. Enemies that are set to appear halfway, and didn't have time to appear in battle, appear after it's done and the battle has no end. Formulas that used to be evaluated just fine suddenly can't be and crash the game. Has anyone experienced anything like this? I am far from an expert, but it seems like maybe something got corrupted along the way and now errors started cropping up. What can I do? Would starting a new project and copying assets and maps and databases help? It would take ages, but I am desperate

posts.author: Ludovinsky
posts.body:
You should always keep multiple backups of your stable project builds. It’s one of the most important habits in game development. Projects can break for all kinds of reasons...even something as simple as a laptop going to sleep mid write can cause file issues. so having clean restore points is the safest long term failsafe.
Before assuming corruption, though, it’s worth doing a structured debug pass. Use F9 during playtesting to inspect your switches and variables midgame, and take notes on what’s behaving correctly and what isn’t. A lot of problems that look like corruption are actually logic issues, event states carrying over from old saves, or plugins not cleaning up properly.
True project corruption in RPG Maker usually means the project won’t load at all, or specific data files fail to parse. If you can still open the editor and run a playtest, then the underlying data is most likely intact. In those cases, debugging your events, plugins, and save files is usually more productive than immediately starting a full port.
Porting to a new project can help if all else fails, but it’s a last resort because of the time involved. I’d only go that route after confirming the issues aren’t coming from switches, variables, plugin order, or old save data.

@Timtrack
That's the thing, I really didn't change much between when things were fine and the sudden glitches. I'm now doing a playthrough to iron things out, making adjustments to enemies, adding a dialogue here and there, nothing major. No new scripts added (except your turn count addon).
The lighting issue happened some time ago, but I thought it was because I used an old save, so I started this playthrough and when I reached that point, it still wasn't working. It's an event which shows a picture that has a light circle around the player and the rest is darker, the picture moving with the player. In the later maps the picture doesn't move with the player, and this also happened when I transferred the player from there to the earlier map. I changed the picture number in the later maps (in the earlier ones it was show picture 1, in the later changed to show picture 2, everything else being the same) and that solved it, but I'm baffled as to why it was a problem (picture 1 always got erased when leaving the dark map).
The save file was a normal save I made, but later it wasn't visible in the loading/saving screen, but was in the Saves directory. When I tried deleting it from the Saves, it said it can't be deleted because it's not there any more. I ended up copying everything except Saves somewhere else and worked on from there.
The formula was in the note window, through Hime's Formula Effects script, and it was supposed to put the actor's ID in a variable. This worked just fine before (and does in a previous backup), but suddenly it can't be evaluated.
About the halfway appear enemies, I thought, too, that it was a script problem (NeonBlack's Victory screen, which has given me some grief before). I tried Yanfly's Victory Aftermath and the same thing happened; however, I did it from an old save, so that might be it (I was frustrated and wasn't thinking straight). I should try from a new one. This issue did not happen always, though, I had a run of 15 battles ending correctly and the 16th got stuck when the enemies appeared. And there's another battle with halfway enemies, which didn't have this issue at all (albeit that one wasn't tested so many times).
@Ludovinsky
That's really good general advice. I mostly do what you suggest.
I do have tons of backups, but it's hard to say which one is the last one without these issues. I was making many small adjustments to many events during this last playthrough and I'm not sure if trying to find all of them wouldn't be more time consuming than just copying everything.
As I said above, there weren't any major changes done to the project. When the problem is with an event, I do check whether the associated switches and variables are what they should be (like with the light event, which should update player's position through variables and move the picture accordingly - the variables were getting updated, but the picture wasn't moving).
I think I'll take a couple of days to cool off and then try again that battle issue with Yanfly's script and a fresh save. But if new weird crashes appear, it's good to know that putting it all in a new project might help. Making this game has been a bright spot in this effed up world and I don't want to lose that.

Click to expand...
Just in case, can you provide the exact formula you were trying to evaluate and in which context?
I ask because by default,
actor_ID
does not exists. (ref to Hime's formula effect
here
if anyone wants to see how it works) So unless you have another script adding this (you can check this by doing CTRL+SHIFT+F in the script editor), then the command will fail.
Note that damage formula do not crash even with invalid commands because the default code will prevent errors and return 0.
If you want to get the actor id and store it into a variable, you should do in Hime's formula:
Code:
v[1] = a.id if a.actor?
or
Code:
v[1] = b.id if b.actor?
Additionally, since Hime's script creates an object before all scripts are loaded (a
Game_Interpreter
here), I suggest you put the script as low as possible in your load order (and above main) to ensure compatibility with scripts modifying the interpreter (I don't believe this will fix your formula issue though).

posts.author: EntangledPear
posts.body:
Well, I calmed down and tried to look at the issues again without the mindset that something fundamental is wrong. I haven't tried the picture fix yet, but looked at the halfway appearing enemies problem. What I found out:
- trying the battles from a new game with Yanfly's Victory Aftermath - same problem: enemies that didn't have a chance to appear, appear after the battle should be done, and if they're defeated, the victory screen (including adding EXP/Gold/drops) appears several times (NeonBlack's victory screen didn't appear at that point at all);
- trying the battles from a new game without any victory screen script - same thing as with Yanfly's, including the multiple victory messages when you beat the re-appeared enemies.
Which leads me to the conclusion that the culprit might be Yami Battle Symphony engine. (Or RPG Maker itself? Probably not.) Or maybe Hime's Post Battle Events? I don't think I have anything else that would mess up battles. I made an unsophisticated fix for this issue - instead of appearing halfway, I made those enemies that should be "summoned" dead before the battle starts and then the summoning enemy revives them instead. It had its own challenges, but it seems to be working for now (tried 40 battles so far). If anyone has ideas about what can be happening about the halfway appearing, I'd be happy to hear them.
I replaced b.actor_id with just b.id (and the crash didn't occur again), but left b.enemy_id, which doesn't seem to be problematic.
I want to thank everyone who replied to me, it really helped me to pull myself together and look for solutions. When (or, hopefully, if) I run into any new issues, I'll make a separate post, but if anyone would like to add anything here, please do.
